stage1Hint1: Count the cells between the robot and the star.
stage1Hint2: How many cells does the robot need to move to reach the star?
stage2Hint1: Look at where the walls are.
stage2Hint2: On which cell should the robot turn to head toward the star?
stage3Hint1: Trace the path the robot can move along.
stage3Hint2: How many corners does the path have, and which way does each one turn?
stage4Hint1: Look at which way the robot is facing.
stage4Hint2: When the robot turns on the first cell, is the star on the robot's right or left?
stage5Hint1: Count the cells on the straight path.
stage5Hint2: You need the same block many times, but you can only use 2 blocks. What can you do?
stage6Hint1: Look at how the stair shape repeats.
stage6Hint2: How many blocks does it take to climb one step? How many times does that happen?
stage7Hint1: Look at the shape the path makes.
stage7Hint2: Did you find the moves for one side? How many times do you need them?
stage8Hint1: Look at the cells left between the end of the stairs and the star.
stage8Hint2: After the repeat ends, is there anything left to do?

prediction.title: Predict
prediction.prompt: Follow the code. Where will the robot stop, and which way will it face?
prediction.incorrect: Not quite. Watch the robot's path again.
prediction.actual: It stopped at row {row}, column {column}, facing {direction}
prediction.firstCheckOpen: First check: the path ahead was open → skipped the inside blocks.
prediction.firstCheckBlocked: First check: the path ahead was blocked → ran the inside blocks.

bonus1Goal: Find the moves that repeat on the bigger stairs.
bonus1Hint1: Compare the flat parts and the climbing parts of the stairs.
bonus1Hint2: On one step, how many cells does the robot move in the same direction? What if you group those moves?
bonus2Title: Bonus 2: A Path with a Start
bonus2Goal: Split the path into the part that repeats and the part that doesn't.
bonus2Hint1: Compare the first part of the path with the part that repeats after it.
bonus2Hint2: Where should you put the move that doesn't fit in the repeating group?
u21Goal: Get through both maps with the same code.
u21Hint1: Compare where the corner is on each map.
u21Hint2: The corners are in different places. How can the robot know when to turn?
u22Goal: This time, turn left when blocked to get through both maps.
u22Hint1: Look at which way the path bends on each map.
u22Hint2: Do you only need to change what happens when blocked, or what you check too?
u23Goal: Use the same code even when there are two corners.
u23Hint1: Find every place where the path bends.
u23Hint2: If you reuse your one-corner idea, how many times should it repeat?
u24Goal: Fix the code that's already there to get through both maps.
u24Hint1: Run the starting code and see which map fails.
u24Hint2: When does if check? Where should if be so it also checks when the wall appears?
u25Goal: Turn when blocked, move when clear — the same code for both maps.
u25Hint1: On map 1, what is in front of the robot at the start?
u25Hint2: If the path is still blocked after one turn, what should happen next?
u26Goal: Get through all three maps with the same code.
u26Hint1: Compare where and how many times the robot must turn on each map.
u26Hint2: In one round of the repeat, should the robot turn and move, or only one of them?
whileName: while the path ahead is clear
whileContinue: The path ahead is clear → continue
whileStop: The path ahead is blocked → stop
whileStepLimit: The loop never ends. Check whether anything inside while changes the condition.
u31Goal: Get through two paths of different lengths with the same code.
u31Hint1: Compare how many cells there are before the first wall on each map.
u31Hint2: To keep going 'until there’s a wall' without counting, which block do you need?
u32Title: Unit 3-2: To the Wall and Turn
u32Goal: Get through two maps where the corners are at different distances.
u32Hint1: Look at how many times 'go to the wall, then turn' repeats.
u32Hint2: If you put while inside repeat, what gets repeated?
u33Title: Unit 3-3: The Loop That Never Ends
u33Goal: Fix the code that never stops and reach the star.
u33Hint1: When you run the starting code, how far does the robot get?
u33Hint2: Can the blocks inside while ever change whether the path ahead is clear?

u41Goal: Make the repeating shape into a function and use it.
u41Hint1: Find how many times the same shape appears on the path.
u41Hint2: What if you could build that shape once and call it many times?
u42Goal: Put repeat inside a function to save blocks.
u42Hint1: Does the shape you’ll make into a function have a repeating part too?
u42Hint2: If you put repeat inside a function, what repeats every time you call it?
u43Title: Unit 4-3: Nothing Happens Until You Call It
u43Goal: Fix the code so the function you made actually runs.
u43Hint1: When you run it, does the robot move?
u43Hint2: Does making a function run it, or do you need to call it?
u51Title: Unit 5-1: As Many as the Box Says
u51Goal: Box A holds a different number on each map. Use the same code for both maps.
u51Hint1: Compare the number in box A with the cells before the turn on each map.
u51Hint2: What happens if you use A instead of a number for the repeat count?
u52Goal: Each part of the path is one cell longer. Change box A as you go to get through both maps.
u52Hint1: How much longer does the path get after each turn?
u52Hint2: If you add 1 to A after each turn, how long will the next part be?
u53Title: Unit 5-3: When the Value Goes In
u53Goal: Fix the code that's already there and reach the star.
u53Hint1: When you run the starting code, how many cells does the robot move?
u53Hint2: When repeat A starts, what number is in box A?

variables.useNumber: Use a number as the count
